sentences.zh: 泻湖中像金枪鱼一样被长矛刺死。

sentences.en: So he advances southwards.
sentences.zh: 如果你是法兰克人，这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: He drives them out from the great fortresses of Arles, of Avignon.
sentences.zh: 到741年，也就是查理·马特尔最终去世的时候，他的军队，即在他领导下的法兰克人，几乎拥有了从比利牛斯山脉一直延伸到多瑙河的土地。

sentences.en: He annihilates a massive seaborne expedition of Omeyad forces outside Narbonne.
sentences.zh: 所以是一片极其广阔的领土。

sentences.en: There's descriptions of the Muslim fugitives trying desperately to swim back to their ships, being pursued by the victorious Franks, being speared in the shallows and
sentences.zh: 所以高卢南部的法兰克领主和倭马亚人，这些人是被查理·马特尔彻底击溃的人，但他们并不孤单。

sentences.en: the lagoons like tuna.
sentences.zh: 法兰克社会中一个非常独特的阶层也是如此。

sentences.en: Fabulous stuff, if you're a Frank.
sentences.zh: 那就是主教们。

sentences.en: And by 741, which is when Charles
sentences.zh: 我们在关于克洛维时代的第一集中谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: Martel finally dies, his armies, so the Franks under his leadership, pretty much have the range of lands stretching from the Pyrenees all the way to the Danube.
sentences.zh: 主教们几乎无一例外都是旧高卢罗马贵族的继承人。

sentences.en: So a vast, vast expanse of territory.
sentences.zh: 那些曾是罗马高卢富裕精英的元老院阶层人物。

sentences.en: So the Frankish lords of southern Gaul and the Omeyads, these are people who've been comprehensively hammered by Charles Martel, but they're not alone.
sentences.zh: 这些家族仍然通过主教制度保持着他们的权威，通过让自己被当地城市选为教区主教。

sentences.en: So too have a very distinctive class in Frankish society.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们能保持影响力。

sentences.en: And these are the bishops.
sentences.zh: 所以查理·马特尔不仅在战场上击败了他们，而且在政治上也压制了他们。

sentences.en: And we talked about this in the first episode we did on, you know, the age of Clovis.
sentences.zh: 他开始没收教会的土地，并将其分发给他的追随者。

sentences.en: The bishops, almost without exception, are the heirs of the kind of the old
sentences.zh: 这在当时是极具争议的。

sentences.en: Gallo-Roman aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 这引起了极大的不满。

sentences.en: The kind of senatorial figures who had been the wealthy elites of Roman
sentences.zh: 但查理·马特尔并不在乎。

sentences.en: Gaul.
sentences.zh: 他需要资源来维持他的军队。

sentences.en: And these families still preserve their authority through the institution of the episcopy, through having themselves elected by their local cities as bishops.
sentences.zh: 这就是他如何建立起那个庞大的帝国的。

sentences.en: You know, if you want an example of a class of people who preserve the traditions of the vanished Roman Empire,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你想找一个能传承消亡的罗马帝国传统的阶层作为例子，

sentences.en: Frankish bishops are your guys.
sentences.zh: 法兰克主教就是你要找的人。

sentences.en: So they're very learned, they're very scholarly, you know, they're kind of educated in classical poetry as well as in the Bible and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们博学多才，很有学术造诣，不仅精通古典诗歌，还通晓《圣经》以及诸如此类的知识。

sentences.en: They may well play a kind of part on the great national stage, but ultimately their real loyalty
sentences.zh: 他们或许在国家大舞台上扮演着某种角色，但归根结底，他们真正的忠诚

sentences.en: isn't to the kind of the distant Frankish king or, you know, in the case of Charles Martel,
sentences.zh: 并不属于那种遥远的法兰克国王，或者像查理·马特（Charles Martel）那种情况，

sentences.en: the distant Frankish mayor, but to the local city, the local community that they represent on the stage of Gaul and whose peoples have elected them.
sentences.zh: 也不属于遥远的法兰克宫相，而是属于他们所代表的那个地方城市、那个地方社区，以及那些在这一高卢舞台上选举他们的人民。

sentences.en: And for the vast majority of Franks, it's the bishops who kind of mediate between the mass of Christians and the dimension of the divine.
sentences.zh: 对于绝大多数法兰克人来说，正是这些主教在广大基督徒与神圣维度之间起到了调解作用。

sentences.en: And they're able to do this because they are almost invariably the descendants of saints and bishops whose tombs are in the cathedrals where they sit.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以能做到这一点，是因为他们几乎无一例外都是圣徒和主教的后裔，而这些圣徒和主教的陵墓就位于他们所驻守的大教堂里。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of family project.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一种家族事业。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the effect of this is that all across Gaul, wherever you go, there are these tombs of martyrs, of holy men, of bishops.
sentences.zh: 其结果就是，无论你走到高卢的哪个角落，到处都有这些殉道者、圣人和主教的陵墓。

sentences.en: I mean, St. Martin is the most famous of these, but he's by no means the only one.
sentences.zh: 我是说，圣马丁（St. Martin）是其中最著名的一位，但绝非唯一的一位。

sentences.en: And it enables the Franks, when they look at their bishops, to feel not just that they have living links with the, you know, the vanished realm of Rome.
sentences.zh: 这使得法兰克人在注视他们的主教时，不仅能感受到他们与那个消亡的罗马帝国之间存在着活生生的联系，

sentences.en: I mean, they don't really care about this by this point, but they can look at their bishops and feel these are venerable
sentences.zh: 我是说，到了这个阶段，他们其实并不在乎这些，但他们看着主教时，会觉得这些人是

sentences.en: representatives of a very, very ancient Christianity.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常古老的基督教的尊贵代表。

sentences.en: And it enables them to feel that Gaul is like a kind of holy land, a Christian holy land.
sentences.zh: 这让他们觉得高卢就像是一片圣地，一片基督教的圣地。

sentences.en: They don't really need, for instance, the sanction of the papacy or whatever.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们并不真正需要教皇之类的认可。

sentences.en: They've got St. Martin.
sentences.zh: 他们有圣马丁。

sentences.en: They've got all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有这一切。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Essentially, they're spiritually self-sufficient.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他们在精神上是自给自足的。

sentences.en: And this has been the case ever since the first emergence of the Frankish monarchy.
sentences.zh: 自法兰克君主制出现以来，情况一直如此。

sentences.en: But the thing about Charles Martel, he doesn't like this at all.
sentences.zh: 但查理·马特的问题在于，他一点也不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: He won't tolerate an alternative power base, presumably.
sentences.zh: 想必他无法容忍一个替代性的权力基础。

sentences.en: Yeah, basically.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上是这样。

sentences.en: He doesn't like these bishops.
sentences.zh: 他不待见这些主教。

sentences.en: They're too independent.
sentences.zh: 他们太独立了。

sentences.en: They're too able to defy his will.
sentences.zh: 他们太有能力违抗他的意志了。

sentences.en: And so what he wants is to replace them with his own kinsmen, with his own trusted allies.
sentences.zh: 所以他想用自己的亲信、自己的心腹来取代他们。

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter to Charles if the bishops he appoints, you know, kind of no Virgil or whatever.
sentences.zh: 对于查理来说，他任命的主教是否懂维吉尔（Virgil）之类的并不重要。

sentences.en: He doesn't care about their educational standards or whether they have local links to the cities that they are going to serve as bishops for,
sentences.zh: 他不在乎他们的教育水平，也不在乎他们是否与即将任职的城市有地方联系，

sentences.en: or if they have family connections to the saints whose tombs lie in their cathedrals.
sentences.zh: 或者他们是否与大教堂里安葬的圣徒有家族渊源。

sentences.en: So that class of person is being elbowed aside.
sentences.zh: 所以那一类人正在被排挤出局。

sentences.en: And Charles is putting in their place, you know, his own henchmen.
sentences.zh: 而查理正在用他自己的爪牙取而代之。

sentences.en: And effectively, this is, I think, the final extinction of Roman
sentences.zh: 实际上，我认为这标志着罗马高卢的

sentences.en: Gaul.
sentences.zh: 最终消亡。

sentences.en: This is where Gaul, if you like, becomes Francia.
sentences.zh: 这就是高卢，如果你愿意的话，变成法兰克尼亚（Francia）的地方。

sentences.en: And Francia is the word that will give us, you know, the name of France.
sentences.zh: 而法兰克尼亚这个词，就是后来法国（France）这个名字的由来。

sentences.en: So you can see Gaul becoming France at this point under the rule of Charles Martel and Patrick Geary, who's the, you know, one of the great historians of this process.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到，在高卢变成法国的这个节点上，在查理·马特和帕特里克·吉里（Patrick Geary）的统治下，而帕特里克·吉里是研究这一进程的伟大历史学家之一。

sentences.en: It's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: So I'll read what he says in full.
sentences.zh: 我来完整读一下他所说的话。

sentences.en: Charles Martel accomplished what no other secular power had been able to do in the previous two centuries by his manipulation of ecclesiastical office.
sentences.zh: 查理·马特通过操纵教会职位，完成了过去两个世纪里任何其他世俗权力都无法做到的事情。

sentences.en: So, you know, getting rid of all these bishops and replacing them with his own men, by the confiscation of the wealth that controlled and by the appointment of ignorant and
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，通过罢免所有这些主教并换上他自己的人，通过没收他们所控制的财富，以及任命那些无知且

sentences.en: entirely worldly lay supporters.
sentences.zh: 完全世俗的平信徒支持者。

sentences.en: He finally succeeded in destroying the religious basis on which had long rested the independent power of the Frankish bishops.
sentences.zh: 他最终成功摧毁了法兰克主教独立权力的宗教基础。

sentences.en: Henceforth, they would be powerful lords at times rivaling in power, dukes, counts, and even kings.
sentences.zh: 此后，他们虽然会成为强大的领主，有时在权力上与公爵、伯爵甚至国王相抗衡，

sentences.en: But they would never again command that particular power as monopolists of the sacred.
sentences.zh: 但他们再也不会像以前那样作为神圣事物的垄断者来行使那种特殊的权力了。

sentences.en: This role, along with the lead in cultural life, would pass to monasteries.
sentences.zh: 这一角色，连同在文化生活中的领导地位，将转交给修道院。

sentences.en: So this is surely a key moment in the transition from late antiquity to early medieval, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这无疑是从古典时代晚期向中世纪早期过渡的关键时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: That they're a vestige of kind of Roman cultural, spiritual life has been smashed.
sentences.zh: 他们作为罗马文化和精神生活遗迹的地位已经被粉碎了。

sentences.en: More power has been concentrated in the hands of the warlords who are now making themselves kings.
sentences.zh: 更多的权力集中到了那些正在自立为王的军阀手中。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，我绝对这么认为。

sentences.en: And what compounds the impact of this process is that in the south of Gaul, where Roman civilization had been much more
sentences.zh: 而且加剧这一进程影响的是，在高卢南部，罗马文明的根基要深厚得多，

sentences.en: deeply planted, it had been there for much longer, urban civilization had kind of survived to a degree that it hadn't in northern Gaul.
sentences.zh: 它在那里存在的时间更长，城市文明在某种程度上得以幸存，而这在北高卢是没有的。

sentences.en: You know, the cities there have, over the previous decades, have been absolutely smashed to pieces, first by the Arab invaders and then by Charles Martel's invasion
sentences.zh: 你知道，那里的城市在过去几十年里被彻底摧毁了，先是遭到阿拉伯入侵者的破坏，然后是查理·马特向

sentences.en: south and his attempt to reclaim these cities.
sentences.zh: 南方的入侵以及他试图收复这些城市的尝试。

sentences.en: So it's not just that the old Roman bishops have been swept aside.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是旧的罗马主教被扫地出门的问题。

sentences.en: It's also that the independence of the cities that had maintained them has also been massively shattered.
sentences.zh: 这也是维持这些城市运作的独立性被彻底粉碎的问题。

sentences.en: So people who've been to the south of France, if you, you know, you think of
sentences.zh: 所以去过法国南部的人，如果你想到

sentences.en: Nîmes or Arles or whatever, there are still incredibly impressive Roman remains there.
sentences.zh: 尼姆（Nîmes）或阿尔勒（Arles）之类的地方，那里仍然有令人印象深刻的罗马遗迹。

sentences.en: But this is the point where they are really starting to crumble away as well, as Roman cities kind of in the north had already done.
sentences.zh: 但这就是它们也开始真正崩塌的时刻，就像北方的罗马城市早已发生的那样。

sentences.en: They start to be cannibalized, they crumble away, they're shattered by wars.
sentences.zh: 它们开始被蚕食，逐渐崩塌，在战争中被摧毁。

sentences.en: And as you say, I think this is really the kind of the end point of late antiquity in Gaul.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我认为这确实是高卢古典时代晚期的终点。

sentences.en: This is where the kind of, if you want to say, the Middle Ages begin.
sentences.zh: 这就是中世纪开始的地方，如果你想这么说的话。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the kind of the start point.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是起点。

sentences.en: And obviously, the bishops, the kind of the Roman old school, the Ancien Régime, they hate this.
sentences.zh: 显然，那些主教，那些罗马老派，那些旧制度（Ancien Régime）的支持者，他们对此恨之入骨。

sentences.en: I mean, they're so resentful.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们太怨恨了。

sentences.en: And there's a perfect example of this in the form of the erstwhile bishop of Orléans, who's a man called Eucarius.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个完美的例子，就是前奥尔良主教，一个叫尤卡里乌斯（Eucarius）的人。

sentences.en: And that's a Roman name.
sentences.zh: 那是一个罗马名字。

sentences.en: And that's really telling, because by this point in the 8th century, most Roman names are fading away.
sentences.zh: 这真的很能说明问题，因为到了8世纪的这个阶段，大多数罗马名字都在逐渐消失。

sentences.en: They're being replaced by Frankish names.
sentences.zh: 它们正在被法兰克名字所取代。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: People are all called Theodore Wolfe or something.
sentences.zh: 人们都叫西奥多·沃尔夫（Theodore Wolfe）之类的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Childebert or whatever.
sentences.zh: 希尔德贝尔特（Childebert）之类的。

sentences.en: But among this kind of class of, you know, descended from senators and so on, they do preserve their Roman name.
sentences.zh: 但在这些出身于元老院议员等阶层的人中，他们确实保留了自己的罗马名字。

sentences.en: So you can tell from Eucarius that he's a kind of very grand figure, you know, with lineage going back to the Roman paSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以从尤卡里乌斯身上看出，他是一个非常显赫的人物，你知道，他的血统可以追溯到罗马的过去。

sentences.en: Anyway, Charles turns up in Orléans after the Battle of Taur, very chipper, very full of himself.
sentences.zh: 总之，图尔战役（Battle of Tours）后，查理出现在奥尔良，兴高采烈，非常自负。

sentences.en: He's beating the enemy off.
sentences.zh: 他击退了敌人。

sentences.en: And Eucarius is kind of grumpy and grouchy and snobbish towards him.
sentences.zh: 而尤卡里乌斯对他表现得既暴躁又傲慢。

sentences.en: So Charles Martell just says, piss off.
sentences.zh: 于是查理·马特直接说，滚开。

sentences.en: Don't want you anymore.
sentences.zh: 不再需要你了。

sentences.en: Replaces him with one of his own henchmen.
sentences.zh: 用他自己的一个心腹取代了他。

sentences.en: And Eucarius is furious about this.
sentences.zh: 尤卡里乌斯对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And in due course, when Charles Martell dies, he reports, he reports a vision that he's been shown in a dream by an angel.
sentences.zh: 后来，当查理·马特去世时，他报告说，他梦见天使向他展示了一个幻象。

sentences.en: And this angel leads Eucarius down into hell.
sentences.zh: 这位天使带领尤卡里乌斯下到了地狱。

sentences.en: And there he shows him Charles Martell condemned in body and soul to eternal punishment.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他向他展示了查理·马特因身心受到的永恒惩罚而被定罪。

sentences.en: And Eucarius wakes up, he's absolutely thrilled by this vision, tells everyone absolutely great news.
sentences.zh: 尤卡里乌斯醒来后，对这个幻象感到非常兴奋，并告诉所有人这绝对是个好消息。

sentences.en: Charles Martell is in hell.
sentences.zh: 查理·马特在地狱里。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, if you want proof for this, let's go to Charles Martell's tomb.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，如果你想要证据，我们去查理·马特的墓地看看。

sentences.en: Let's open it up and see if the body's there.
sentences.zh: 让我们打开它，看看尸体还在不在。

sentences.en: Because if it's not away and dunked in the, you know, the boiling vats of the inferno.
sentences.zh: 因为如果不在了，那肯定是被扔进地狱的沸腾大锅里了。

sentences.en: So a party got together, they go to Charles's tomb, they open it up.
sentences.zh: 于是大家聚在一起，来到查理的墓前，打开了它。

sentences.en: And I will quote from a subsequent record of what happens.
sentences.zh: 我将引用随后发生的事情的记录。

sentences.en: Therefore, they went to the aforementioned monastery where Charles's body was buried.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们去了上述查理尸体被埋葬的修道院。

sentences.en: They opened his tomb and suddenly, Dominic, a dragon emerged.
sentences.zh: 他们打开了他的坟墓，突然，多米尼克，一条龙出现了。

sentences.en: Oh my words.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And the whole interior of the tomb was found to be blackened as if it had been burned.
sentences.zh: 整个墓穴内部被发现一片漆黑，仿佛被烧过一样。

sentences.en: And that actually happened.
sentences.zh: 而这确实发生了。

sentences.en: Well, right at the beginning of this series, in the episode we did on Clavers, I promised people that we'd have a dragon.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在这个系列节目刚开始时，在我们制作的关于克拉弗斯（Clavers）的那一集里，我向大家承诺过我们会有一条龙。

sentences.en: And there it is.
sentences.zh: 看，它就在那儿。

sentences.en: And now we have.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了。

sentences.en: Comes rushing out.
sentences.zh: 它冲了出来。

sentences.en: It's obviously been burning the tomb.
sentences.zh: 显然它一直在焚烧坟墓。

sentences.en: Charles Martell's body has been taken, dunked in hell.
sentences.zh: 查理·马特的尸体已经被带走，扔进了地狱。

sentences.en: What more proof do you need?
sentences.zh: 你还需要什么证据？

sentences.en: Okay, well, that's good enough for me.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这对我来说已经足够了。

sentences.en: Okay, but not everybody in the church thinks Charles is a bad guy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但教会里并非所有人都认为查理是个坏人。

sentences.en: And in fact, there are bishops who think, oh, he's brilliant, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 事实上，有些主教认为他很棒，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's one very particular bishop, and that is the Bishop of Rome.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一位非常特别的主教，那就是罗马主教。

sentences.en: Rome, the Pope.
sentences.zh: 罗马，教皇。

sentences.en: So the Pope from Rome, I mean, he has no particular dog in the fight.
sentences.zh: 所以来自罗马的教皇，我是说，他在这场争斗中没有特别的立场。

sentences.en: He doesn't mind at all what Charles Martell is doing to the bishops in Gaul.
sentences.zh: 他一点也不介意查理·马特对高卢的主教们做了什么。

sentences.en: And in fact, he's very, very keen to cozy up to Charles Martell.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他非常、非常渴望与查理·马特套近乎。

sentences.en: So in 739, which is two years before Charles dies, the Pope, who's called Gregory III, sends him the keys of St. Peter and a portion of the chains
sentences.zh: 所以在739年，也就是查理去世前两年，教皇格列高利三世（Gregory III）送给他圣彼得的钥匙和一部分锁链，

sentences.en: that had bound St. Peter when he was held in prison before being executed by the Romans.
sentences.zh: 这些锁链是圣彼得在被罗马人处决前被囚禁时所戴的。

sentences.en: And this is a pretty clear signal that the papacy is interested in doing a deal with Charles and with his family.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常明确的信号，表明教皇有兴趣与查理及其家族达成协议。

sentences.en: And this is quite timely because everyone knows that Charles isn't long for this life.
sentences.zh: 而且这非常及时，因为大家都知道查理时日无多了。

sentences.en: You know, by 739, he's pretty old.
sentences.zh: 你知道，到了739年，他已经很老了。

sentences.en: And the assumption is that Charles's two eldest sons, one of whom is called
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为查理的两个长子，一个叫

sentences.en: Carloman, one of whom is called Pepin, will succeed him.
sentences.zh: 卡洛曼（Carloman），一个叫丕平（Pepin），将继承他的位置。

sentences.en: But they will do so, obviously, not as kings, but as mayors.
sentences.zh: 但显然，他们不会以国王的身份，而是以宫相的身份继位。

sentences.en: And I think there's a sense, not just in Rome, but also across, you know, most of the Frankish kingdom, that this is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 我认为不仅在罗马，而且在整个法兰克王国，人们都觉得这很荒谬。

sentences.en: I mean, it's mad that, you know, you've still got a Merovingian king with his long hair and he's being wheeled out on his cart and that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太疯狂了，你仍然有一个留着长发的墨洛温王朝国王，他被用车推出来展示，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And this is focused when Charles dies in 741.
sentences.zh: 当查理在741年去世时，这一点变得更加突出。

sentences.en: And sure enough, his roles as mayor are divided up among his sons.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，他作为宫相的角色被分给了他的儿子们。

sentences.en: So the elder one, Carloman, becomes the mayor of Austrasia, the Eastern Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 长子卡洛曼成为了奥斯特拉西亚（Austrasia，东王国）的宫相。

sentences.en: And the younger one, Pepin, becomes the mayor of Neustria with his capital now based in Paris.
sentences.zh: 次子丕平成为了纽斯特里亚（Neustria）的宫相，首都现在设在巴黎。

sentences.en: And what makes this even more ridiculous and seem ludicrous to people is that there isn't even at this point a Merovingian king on the throne.
sentences.zh: 而让这一切显得更加荒唐可笑的是，此时王位上甚至连一个墨洛温王朝的国王都没有了。

sentences.en: They've run out of Merovingians.
sentences.zh: 他们的墨洛温人已经用完了。

sentences.en: They've run out of Merovingians.
sentences.zh: 他们的墨洛温人已经用完了。

sentences.en: They haven't got one.
sentences.zh: 他们一个都没有了。

sentences.en: So Carloman and Pepin, it's difficult for them initially to establish their authority.
sentences.zh: 所以卡洛曼和丕平起初很难确立他们的权威。

sentences.en: They're not the hammer.
sentences.zh: 他们不是“铁锤”。

sentences.en: So it takes some time to affirm their authority.
sentences.zh: 所以需要一些时间来巩固他们的权威。

sentences.en: They think, well, actually, maybe it would be kind of easier for us if we did have a kind of Merovingian king on the throne.
sentences.zh: 他们想，嗯，实际上，如果我们王位上有一个墨洛温王朝的国王，也许对我们来说会更容易一些。

sentences.en: So they look around and they find a Merovingian and he's a guy called Chilperic.
sentences.zh: 于是他们四处寻找，找到了一个墨洛温人，他叫希尔德里克（Chilperic）。

sentences.en: Inevitably.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地。

sentences.en: And they plonk him on the throne and he becomes Chilperic III.
sentences.zh: 他们把他推上王位，他成为了希尔德里克三世。

sentences.en: But the obvious solution to this whole problem is for him to be deposed, for the Merovingian monarchy itself to be abolished,
sentences.zh: 但解决这个问题的显而易见的办法是废黜他，废除墨洛温王朝本身，

sentences.en: and for either Carloman or Pepin or perhaps both to become kings.
sentences.zh: 并让卡洛曼或丕平，或者两者都成为国王。

sentences.en: But there is a problem, which is, you know, how do you do this?
sentences.zh: 但有一个问题，就是，你知道，你怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Because Clovis, when he'd become king, you know, this is why he'd proclaimed himself Augustus and why he'd boasted about, you know, his long hair
sentences.zh: 因为克洛维（Clovis）在成为国王时，你知道，这就是他宣称自己为奥古斯都的原因，也是他吹嘘自己留着长发

sentences.en: and being descended from a weird sea monster.
sentences.zh: 以及是海怪后裔的原因。

sentences.en: If you're going to be a king, you need a source of legitimacy because you need to demonstrate to your people and be confident in your own heart,
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为国王，你需要一个合法性的来源，因为你需要向你的人民证明，并且在自己的内心、

sentences.en: in your own soul, that God approves of your elevation to the throne.
sentences.zh: 在自己的灵魂深处确信，上帝认可你登上王位。

sentences.en: So you need something or perhaps someone who can provide that legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要某种东西，或者也许是某个人，能够提供这种合法性。

sentences.en: Who on earth would that be?
sentences.zh: 那到底会是谁呢？

sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》。

sentences.en: We ended with one of the great cliffhangers, not merely in the history of this podcast, but I think in the history of probably all human civilization.
sentences.zh: 我们以一个伟大的悬念结束了上一期，这不仅是本播客历史上，我认为也是整个人类文明史上最伟大的悬念之一。

sentences.en: Who or what is the possible source of authority that could bestow kingship on Karl-Aman and Pepin, these people who are ruling Austrasia and Neustria in the realm of the Franks?
sentences.zh: 究竟是谁或什么权威，能够赋予卡尔曼和丕平——这些统治着法兰克王国奥斯特拉西亚和纽斯特里亚的人——国王的身份？

sentences.en: I mean, massive questions.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这可是个宏大的问题。

sentences.en: A massive question, and you gave a little spoiler, I felt.
sentences.zh: 一个宏大的问题，而且我觉得你刚才稍微剧透了一下。

sentences.en: Disappointingly, you said our eyes would be turning to Rome.
sentences.zh: 令人失望的是，你说我们的目光将转向罗马。

sentences.en: So, tell us, who is this person?
sentences.zh: 那么，告诉我们，此人是谁？

sentences.en: Well, of course, Rome is the home of the papacy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，罗马是教皇的所在地。

sentences.en: And people who have listened who got this far in the series may have noticed we haven't really mentioned the papacy much.
sentences.zh: 听过这期节目并追到这里的听众可能已经注意到，我们之前并没有怎么提到过教皇。

sentences.en: And I guess, Dominic, lots of people may have the sense that the Pope is the key player in medieval Europe and therefore kind of find it a bit weird.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我想很多人可能觉得教皇是中世纪欧洲的关键人物，所以会觉得这有点奇怪。

sentences.en: But at this point, the authority and the influence of the papacy are just a shadow of what they will become kind of in due course over the course of the high Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，教皇的权威和影响力与他在中世纪盛期即将达到的高度相比，简直是小巫见大巫。

sentences.en: So, the Bishop of Rome, the Pope, I mean, he is kind of widely acknowledged by other churchmen across the West as being the most senior.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗马主教，也就是教皇，他在西方各地的教会人士眼中，确实被公认为地位最高。

sentences.en: He's the most senior bishop.
sentences.zh: 他是地位最高的教长。

sentences.en: But that's about the limit of it.
sentences.zh: 但也就仅限于此了。

sentences.en: So, if the Pope, you know, he writes to kings, you know, he'll get their respect, they'll hear him out, but they won't necessarily obey him.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果教皇写信给国王，他会得到他们的尊重，他们会听取他的意见，但不一定会服从他。

sentences.en: He can offer them advice, but he certainly can't kind of give them orders.
sentences.zh: 他可以提供建议，但绝对无法下达命令。

sentences.en: And part of that is because he would never think of doing it.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他根本没想过要这么做。

sentences.en: I mean, it wouldn't cross his mind that that's his role.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他根本不会想到那是他的职责。

sentences.en: But also, even if he did, you know, he lacks the means to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且即便他想做，他也缺乏相应的手段。

sentences.en: As we said, the bishops, say, in Gaul are very independent.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，高卢的主教们非常独立。

sentences.en: They don't see themselves as being under the thumb of the Bishop of Rome.
sentences.zh: 他们并不认为自己受制于罗马主教。

sentences.en: So, the Franks, I think they respect him, the Pope, but not much more than that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为法兰克人尊重教皇，但也仅止于此。

sentences.en: And definitely, you know, the bishops in Gaul, these kind of grand descendants of senators, they don't.
sentences.zh: 而且毫无疑问，高卢的那些主教，那些元老院议员的显赫后裔们，他们并不买账。

sentences.en: They don't feel any sense of cultural cringe towards Rome.
sentences.zh: 他们对罗马没有任何文化上的自卑感。

sentences.en: You know, they don't need him.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要他。

sentences.en: They are their own men.
sentences.zh: 他们有自己的主见。

sentences.en: They have their own saints.
sentences.zh: 他们有自己的圣徒。

sentences.en: They have their own traditions.
sentences.zh: 他们有自己的传统。

sentences.en: They are what they are.
sentences.zh: 他们就是他们自己。

sentences.en: And the truth is that just as the Franks aren't particularly interested in the Bishop of Rome, the Bishop of Rome isn't really very interested in the Franks.
sentences.zh: 事实是，正如法兰克人对罗马主教不怎么感兴趣一样，罗马主教对法兰克人其实也没什么兴趣。

sentences.en: Because in Rome, you still have this kind of inheritance of ancient assumptions that anyone north of the Alps is a complete barbarian.
sentences.zh: 因为在罗马，人们依然保留着一种古老的假设，认为阿尔卑斯山以北的所有人都是彻头彻尾的野蛮人。

sentences.en: I mean, the Franks are, you know, they still see them as these kind of awful people with enormous moustaches and tight pants and stuff.
sentences.zh: 法兰克人在他们眼中，依然是那种留着大胡子、穿着紧身裤之类的可怕家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, they're not entirely wrong, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 说实话，他们说得也没错。

sentences.en: But it's also because, to be honest, for most of the period that we've been describing, the popes have a lot on their plate.
sentences.zh: 但这也是因为，老实说，在我们描述的大部分时期里，教皇们自己都忙得不可开交。

sentences.en: So they have much more pressing things to worry about than, you know, what might be going on in Paris or Toulouse or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们有更紧迫的事情要操心，而不是巴黎或图卢兹等地发生了什么。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that they are still a part of the Roman Empire that is centered in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，他们仍然是君士坦丁堡为中心的罗马帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: So the Roman Empire in the west has fallen, but there is still an Eastern Roman Empire, the Byzantine Empire, as it's often called.
sentences.zh: 西罗马帝国虽然灭亡了，但东罗马帝国，也就是通常所说的拜占庭帝国，依然存在。

sentences.en: And back in the 6th century, so that's around the time that Fredegund and Brunhilde are being born.
sentences.zh: 回到6世纪，也就是弗雷德贡德和布伦希尔德出生的那个时代。

sentences.en: The great emperor Justinian, not really a friend of the show, is he?
sentences.zh: 伟大的皇帝查士丁尼，他算不上我们节目的朋友，对吧？

sentences.en: But his wife, Theodora, is definitely a friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 但他妻子狄奥多拉绝对是我们节目的朋友。

sentences.en: Is he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Theodora, definitely a friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 狄奥多拉，绝对是我们节目的朋友。

sentences.en: Erstwhile star of Love Island, winner of Love Island, in fact.
sentences.zh: 她是《恋爱岛》的前明星，事实上还是《恋爱岛》的冠军。

sentences.en: Anyway, Justinian had sent a great invasion force to reconquer Rome.
sentences.zh: 总之，查士丁尼曾派遣一支庞大的入侵部队去收复罗马。

sentences.en: And that had up to a degree been successful.
sentences.zh: 在一定程度上，这确实成功了。

sentences.en: Rome had been incorporated back into the Byzantine Empire.
sentences.zh: 罗马被重新并入了拜占庭帝国。

sentences.en: And this had been quite humiliating for the Romans because they had been the original imperial capital and the Byzantines acknowledged Rome as the older city.
sentences.zh: 这对罗马人来说相当屈辱，因为他们原本是帝国首都，拜占庭人也承认罗马是更古老的城市。

sentences.en: But they also said that compared to Constantinople, it counts as the lesser city.
sentences.zh: 但他们同时也说，与君士坦丁堡相比，罗马只能算是次要城市。

sentences.en: And so the people of Rome who were once the rulers of this great empire are now themselves kind of subjects.
sentences.zh: 所以，曾经统治这个伟大帝国的罗马人民，现在自己也成了臣民。

sentences.en: And the inferiority of Rome to Constantinople is institutionalized in the wake of its reconquest by Justinian's armies.
sentences.zh: 在查士丁尼军队收复罗马后，罗马相对于君士坦丁堡的从属地位被制度化了。

sentences.en: So you have a Byzantine governor installed not in Rome, but in Ravenna to rule Byzantine
sentences.zh: 所以，拜占庭派驻的总督不是在罗马，而是在拉文纳统治拜占庭意大利。

sentences.en: Italy.
sentences.zh: 意大利。

sentences.en: But Ravenna, to be fair, had been an imperial capital for a while.
sentences.zh: 但平心而论，拉文纳也曾做过一段时间的帝国首都。

sentences.en: It had.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But I mean, it's embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这很尴尬。

sentences.en: Rome is not just a provincial capital.
sentences.zh: 罗马不仅不再是行省首府。

sentences.en: It's not even a capital at all.
sentences.zh: 它甚至根本算不上首都。

sentences.en: The emperor kind of lavishes Byzantine titles on the Roman aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 皇帝将各种拜占庭头衔赐予罗马贵族。

sentences.en: Byzantine fashions become all the rage.
sentences.zh: 拜占庭时尚变得风靡一时。

sentences.en: People speak Greek.
sentences.zh: 人们开始说希腊语。

sentences.en: There are Greek churches set up in Rome.
sentences.zh: 罗马建立了希腊教堂。

sentences.en: And Rome becomes essentially a kind of ersatz version of Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 罗马本质上变成了一个山寨版的君士坦丁堡。

sentences.en: And for the bishop of Rome, again, there are kind of constant reminders of his inferior status.
sentences.zh: 对于罗马主教来说，他也不断地被提醒着自己低下的地位。

sentences.en: So every time he celebrates a mass, he prays for his absent master, the emperor in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 每次做弥撒时，他都要为他远方的君主——君士坦丁堡的皇帝祈祷。

sentences.en: Every time he writes a letter, he's dating it by the regnal year, again, of the emperor in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 每次写信，他都要用君士坦丁堡皇帝的在位年份来标注日期。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, as he sits there in Rome, whether he's kind of wandering through the forum or going
sentences.zh: 与此同时，当他坐在罗马时，无论是在广场漫步，还是在战神广场散步，

sentences.en: for a walk on the campus Martius, all around him, you get in this very memorable phrase by Peter Brown, the great historian of late antiquity, he hears all around him the crash
sentences.zh: 正如晚期古典时代伟大的历史学家彼得·布朗那句令人难忘的话所说，他周围听到的全是

sentences.en: of falling masonry.
sentences.zh: 建筑坍塌的轰鸣声。

sentences.en: So ancient Rome is literally falling to pieces around the pope.
sentences.zh: 所以，古罗马在教皇身边正一点点分崩离析。

sentences.en: But the pope is not entirely devoid of assets, is he?
sentences.zh: 但教皇并非一无所有，对吧？

sentences.en: He's got his spiritual assets.
sentences.zh: 他拥有精神资产。

sentences.en: He's still a prestigious person.
sentences.zh: 他依然是一个享有盛誉的人。

sentences.en: He's still the preeminent head of any church in the Christian world, right?
sentences.zh: 他依然是基督教世界中任何教会的杰出领袖，对吧？

sentences.en: He's got a palace that was given to the papacy by Constantine.
sentences.zh: 他拥有一座君士坦丁大帝赠予教皇的宫殿。

sentences.zh: 一个超越普通人的人，这是墨洛温王朝从未面临过的挑战，因为墨洛温王朝可以声称他们是某种奇怪的

sentences.en: sea monster.
sentences.zh: 海怪的后裔。

sentences.en: They had their long hair.
sentences.zh: 他们留着长发。

sentences.en: They had all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有所有这些东西。

sentences.en: Pepin doesn't have any of this.
sentences.zh: 丕平没有这些。

sentences.en: So what he does is he turns to the Bible.
sentences.zh: 所以他转向了《圣经》。

sentences.en: And in the Bible, he reads of people who had not been of royal stock being elevated to the throne.
sentences.zh: 在《圣经》中，他读到了非王室血统的人被提升到王位的故事。

sentences.en: David.
sentences.zh: 大卫。

sentences.en: Saul and David being the classic examples.
sentences.zh: 扫罗和大卫就是典型的例子。

sentences.en: And the mark of their becoming kings is that they are anointed with holy oil.
sentences.zh: 他们成为国王的标志是他们被涂抹了圣油。

sentences.en: And so this is what Pepin has done to himself.
sentences.zh: 这就是丕平对自己所做的事情。

sentences.en: Goes to Soissons in Neustria, northeast of Francia.
sentences.zh: 他前往纽斯特里亚的苏瓦松，法兰克东北部。

sentences.en: And there the holy oil is put on his brow by a bishop.
sentences.zh: 在那里，一位主教将圣油涂在他的额头上。

sentences.en: And he feels it kind of impregnating his skin.
sentences.zh: 他感觉到它渗入了他的皮肤。

sentences.en: And he has been elevated to a kind of sacramental level.
sentences.zh: 他被提升到了某种圣礼的层面。

sentences.en: And then three years later, he goes one better.
sentences.zh: 三年后，他更进一步。

sentences.en: And he gets the pope himself to come to Francia to repeat this ceremony.
sentences.zh: 他让教皇亲自来到法兰克王国重复这个仪式。

sentences.en: And by this point, Zachary is dead.
sentences.zh: 到那时，扎卡里已经去世了。

sentences.en: But there is a new pope called Stephen II.
sentences.zh: 但有一位新教皇，名叫斯蒂芬二世。

sentences.en: And he is more than ready to do as Pepin wants, basically to answer the Frankish king's bidding.
sentences.zh: 他非常乐意按照丕平的要求去做，基本上是响应法兰克国王的号召。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that the Lombards are still very much on the scene.
sentences.zh: 原因在于伦巴第人依然活跃。

sentences.en: So in the autumn of 754, he sets off from Rome northwards towards the Alps.
sentences.zh: 因此，在754年的秋天，他从罗马出发，向北前往阿尔卑斯山。

sentences.en: And he is the first pope ever to travel to Gaul, to travel beyond the Alps.
sentences.zh: 他是第一位前往高卢、越过阿尔卑斯山的教皇。

sentences.en: And there's a very dramatic account of his journey.
sentences.zh: 关于他的旅程有非常戏剧性的描述。

sentences.en: I mean, it really does read like something out of Lord of the Rings, some kind of fantasy novel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，读起来真的很像《指环王》之类的奇幻小说。

sentences.en: There's descriptions of him climbing the Alps amid gusts of snow.
sentences.zh: 书中描述他在阵阵风雪中攀登阿尔卑斯山。

sentences.en: And he's following a kind of ancient Roman road that's been left all cracked and overgrown by centuries of disrepair.
sentences.zh: 他沿着一条古老的罗马道路前行，由于几个世纪的失修，道路已经破裂且杂草丛生。

sentences.en: And he travels through a great wilderness of kind of sickening mists and ice.
sentences.zh: 他穿过一片令人作呕的迷雾和冰雪的荒野。

sentences.en: And finally, he reaches the summit of the pass.
sentences.zh: 最终，他到达了山口的顶峰。

sentences.en: And this is the gateway of the kingdom of the Franks.
sentences.zh: 这是法兰克王国的门户。

sentences.en: But below him, so below the road, there is this great frozen lake.
sentences.zh: 但在他下方，也就是道路下方，有一个巨大的冰封湖泊。

sentences.en: And beside it, there's the ruins of a long abandoned pagan temple.
sentences.zh: 旁边还有一座早已废弃的异教神庙的废墟。

sentences.en: And, you know, for Stephen II coming from Rome, this is, you know, he thinks, what am I doing?
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于从罗马来的斯蒂芬二世来说，他心想：我在做什么？

sentences.en: This is a terrible mistake.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可怕的错误。

sentences.en: But then he continues down the road into the land of the Franks.
sentences.zh: 但随后他继续沿着道路进入了法兰克人的土地。

sentences.en: And he very soon reaches an abbey that had been sacred to an entire legion of Christians who had been martyred by the Romans back in the days of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 他很快到达了一座修道院，那里曾供奉着一整支在罗马帝国时期被罗马人殉道的基督徒军团。

sentences.en: And his hosts tell the pope that there is no people in the world who are more devoted to the cult of the martyrs, to the cult of the saints than the Franks.
sentences.zh: 他的东道主告诉教皇，世界上没有比法兰克人更崇拜殉道者、更崇拜圣徒的民族了。

sentences.en: And the pope is told, the bodies of the holy martyrs, which the Romans had buried with fire and mutilated by the sword and torn apart by throwing them to wild beasts, these bodies
sentences.zh: 教皇被告知，那些被罗马人用火焚烧、用剑残害、被扔给野兽撕碎的圣殉道者的遗体，

sentences.en: they had found and enclosed in gold and precious stones.
sentences.zh: 他们已经找到并用黄金和宝石包裹起来了。

sentences.en: So it's actually pretty passive aggressive because what they're doing is saying, we don't really need you.
sentences.zh: 这实际上相当消极怠工，因为他们是在说：我们并不真正需要你。

sentences.en: We've got our own saints.
sentences.zh: 我们有自己的圣徒。

sentences.en: We are kind of holier than the Romans.
sentences.zh: 我们比罗马人更神圣。

sentences.en: And, you know, you're the bishop of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 而且，你是罗马人的主教。

sentences.en: So, you know, just remember.
sentences.zh: 所以，记住这一点。

sentences.en: What does the pope make of this?
sentences.zh: 教皇对此有何看法？

sentences.en: I don't think the pope really notices what he's being told because I think he's so relieved that he's managed to get across the Alps.
sentences.zh: 我觉得教皇并没有真正留意别人对他说了什么，因为他能成功翻越阿尔卑斯山，这让他感到如释重负。

sentences.en: He hasn't fallen into a ravine.
sentences.zh: 他没有掉进深谷。

sentences.en: He hasn't been attacked by the phantoms of pagan gods that he's just glad to be among civilized Christian people.
sentences.zh: 他没有受到那些异教神灵幻影的攻击，所以他只是很高兴能置身于文明的基督徒中间。

sentences.en: And so he continues on his way.
sentences.zh: 于是他继续前行。

sentences.en: It takes him six weeks.
sentences.zh: 他花了六个星期。

sentences.en: He gets to Paris and there he meets Pepin and he sees Pepin and he immediately kind of bursts into ostentatious floods of tears.
sentences.zh: 他到达巴黎，在那里见到了丕平。当他看到丕平时，立刻就有些情不自禁地泪流满面。

sentences.en: And he begs Pepin to come to the protection of St. Peter.
sentences.zh: 他恳求丕平来保护圣彼得。

sentences.en: And then he goes with Pepin up to the great abbey of Saint-Denis, which is where Charles
sentences.zh: 然后他与丕平一同前往圣但尼大修道院，那里是查理

sentences.en: Martel had been buried.
sentences.zh: 马特被安葬的地方。

sentences.en: Obviously, where the dragon had been hanging out.
sentences.zh: 显然，那也是那条“龙”曾经盘踞的地方。

sentences.en: And there in Saint-Denis, he anoints him a second time.
sentences.zh: 在圣但尼，他第二次为丕平涂油加冕。

sentences.en: And just for good measure, he salutes not just Pepin as the anointed king of God, but the Franks themselves as the new Israelites.
sentences.zh: 为了保险起见，他不仅向被涂油的上帝之王丕平致敬，还向法兰克人本身致敬，称他们为新的以色列人。

sentences.en: He hails them as a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a peculiar people.
sentences.zh: 他称赞他们是“被拣选的族类，是有君尊的祭司，是圣洁的国度，是属神的子民”。

sentences.en: So essentially, the Pope is now lending his prestige to the self-conceit of the Franks that they are, you know, they are something special.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，教皇现在是在利用自己的威望，来满足法兰克人那种自负的心理，让他们觉得自己确实与众不同。

sentences.en: And so do the Franks live up to their side of their bargain?
sentences.zh: 那么，法兰克人是否履行了他们的承诺呢？

sentences.en: Because obviously he's looking to them to protect him against the Lombards, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，他指望他们保护他免受伦巴第人的侵害，不是吗？

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He absolutely lives up to his side of the bargain.
sentences.zh: 他绝对履行了自己的承诺。

sentences.en: So 755, one year after he's been anointed by the Pope, he crosses the Alps, he invades
sentences.zh: 所以在755年，也就是他被教皇涂油加冕一年后，他翻越阿尔卑斯山，入侵了

sentences.en: Lombardy, he smashes the Lombard king, gets the Lombard king to submit.
sentences.zh: 伦巴第，击溃了伦巴第国王，迫使伦巴第国王屈服。

sentences.en: Two years later, the Lombards are causing trouble again.
sentences.zh: 两年后，伦巴第人又开始制造麻烦。

sentences.en: So Pepin returns to northern Italy, inflicts an even more crushing defeat on the Lombards.
sentences.zh: 于是丕平回到意大利北部，对伦巴第人进行了更沉重的打击。

sentences.en: And this time, all the territories that the Lombards had conquered from Byzantium are given by Pepin to the Pope, or rather to St. Peter, but effectively to the Pope.
sentences.zh: 这一次，伦巴第人从拜占庭征服的所有领土，都被丕平赠予了教皇，或者说是赠予了圣彼得，但实际上是给了教皇。

sentences.en: And Pepin then goes down to Rome and he has all the keys of the cities that he's conquered and he lays them on the tomb of St. Peter, on the tomb of the apostle.
sentences.zh: 随后，丕平前往罗马，他带着所有被征服城市的钥匙，将它们放在了圣彼得的墓前，放在了使徒的墓前。

sentences.en: And of course, as St. Peter's caretaker is the Pope, so effectively the Pope is now the
sentences.zh: 当然，由于圣彼得的看护人就是教皇，所以实际上，教皇现在成了

sentences.en: master of this great swathe of lands that previously had been ruled by the emperor in Constantinople and then had been purloined by the Lombard king.
sentences.zh: 这片广袤土地的主人，这些土地以前由君士坦丁堡的皇帝统治，后来被伦巴第国王窃取了。

sentences.en: And the news of this, when it reaches Constantinople, I mean, the emperor is absolutely furious.
sentences.zh: 当这个消息传到君士坦丁堡时，皇帝简直愤怒到了极点。

sentences.en: He says, these are mine.
sentences.zh: 他说，这些都是我的。

sentences.en: But the Pope, you know, he doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 但教皇并不在乎。

sentences.en: He shifted his loyalty.
sentences.zh: 他已经改变了立场。

sentences.en: He's no longer team Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 他不再站在君士坦丁堡这一边了。

sentences.en: He's now very much team Frank.
sentences.zh: 他现在完全是法兰克阵营的了。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that Pepin and the Franks have, you know, plucked him and the papacy from the absolute jaws of disaster.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，丕平和法兰克人将他和教廷从绝对的灾难边缘拉了回来。

sentences.en: And God's hand is also evident in the greatness of Pepin in the wake of his anointing, because
sentences.zh: 上帝的旨意在丕平加冕后的伟大成就中也显而易见，因为

sentences.en: following Stephen's arrival in Paris and his hailing of the Franks as a holy people, everything goes absolutely brilliantly for them, absolutely amazingly.
sentences.zh: 在斯蒂芬抵达巴黎并称赞法兰克人为圣洁的民族之后，他们的一切都进行得非常顺利，简直令人惊叹。

sentences.en: And in fact, by the time that Pepin dies in 768, he has set the Frankish monarchy and the
sentences.zh: 事实上，到768年丕平去世时，他已经为法兰克君主制和

sentences.en: Frankish empire on even more solid and impressive foundations than Charles Martel has done.
sentences.zh: 法兰克帝国奠定了比查理·马特时期更加稳固和令人印象深刻的基础。

sentences.en: So the taming of the Lombards is only one of Pepin's triumphs.
sentences.zh: 所以，驯服伦巴第人只是丕平的功绩之一。

sentences.en: He also effectively clears the Arabs from the south of Francia, kind of expels them beyond the Pyrenees.
sentences.zh: 他还实际上将阿拉伯人从法兰克南部清除出去，将他们驱逐到了比利牛斯山脉之外。

sentences.en: Aquitaine is also absolutely and definitively reduced to obedience.
sentences.zh: 阿基坦也彻底且最终地被迫服从。

sentences.en: So I said that Odo, the great duke of Aquitaine, who'd fought with Charles Martel at tour, he's
sentences.zh: 我曾提到过，曾与查理·马特并肩作战的阿基坦大公奥多，他已经

sentences.en: retired to a monastery, but his son and his grandson had tried to continue the struggle,
sentences.zh: 退隐到修道院，但他的儿子和孙子曾试图继续抗争，

sentences.en: Pepin not having any of it.
sentences.zh: 丕平根本不吃这一套。

sentences.en: The last duke of Aquitaine, Odo's grandson, gets murdered by his own followers because they think he's such a loser.
sentences.zh: 阿基坦的最后一位公爵，也就是奥多的孙子，被他自己的追随者谋杀了，因为他们觉得他是个彻头彻尾的失败者。

sentences.en: And after that, there's no more talk of an independent Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，再也没有人谈论阿基坦独立了。

sentences.en: The whole while, Pepin has continued Charles Martel's devotion to military discipline.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，丕平一直延续着查理·马特对军事纪律的重视。

sentences.en: He's recruited more heavy cavalry.
sentences.zh: 他招募了更多的重骑兵。

sentences.en: He's gragooned his infantry so that they're on absolute peak of discipline and fitness and expertise.
sentences.zh: 他训练了他的步兵，使他们达到了纪律、体能和专业技能的巅峰。

sentences.en: He continues to sponsor missionary work on the eastern flank of his empire among the pagan Germans.
sentences.zh: 他继续资助帝国东部边境异教徒日耳曼人中间的传教工作。

sentences.en: And all of which means that when he dies, he leaves to his two eldest sons.
sentences.zh: 所有这些意味着，当他去世时，他留给了他的两个长子。

sentences.en: The elder one is called Charles.
sentences.zh: 长子叫查理。

sentences.en: The younger one, confusingly, is called Carloman.
sentences.zh: 次子叫卡洛曼，这名字容易让人混淆。

sentences.en: Absolute waves of Carlomans in this episode.
sentences.zh: 这一集里到处都是叫卡洛曼的人。

sentences.en: But he leaves to them a kingdom that's not just the foremost power in Western Europe, but is obviously absolutely primed to become even more formidable.
sentences.zh: 但他留给他们的王国，不仅是西欧的首要强权，而且显然已经准备好变得更加强大。

sentences.en: You know, everything is ready for even more impressive conquests.
sentences.zh: 一切都已就绪，可以进行更令人印象深刻的征服。

sentences.en: But there's an obvious problem.
sentences.zh: 但有一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: This issue of two sons.
sentences.zh: 两个儿子的继承问题。

sentences.en: So the Franks have a history of dividing up their realms to avoid fighting, to divide them up between different brothers.
sentences.zh: 法兰克人有分割领土的传统，以避免兄弟间的争斗，将领土分给不同的兄弟。

sentences.en: And when you've got two brothers here, Charles and Carloman, is there not an enormous latent
sentences.zh: 现在有两个兄弟，查理和卡洛曼，难道没有巨大的潜在

sentences.en: potential for a civil war between the two of them?
sentences.zh: 内战风险吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Pepin and the elder Carloman, they got on well.
sentences.zh: 丕平和年长的卡洛曼相处得很好。

sentences.en: Carloman, the guy who goes off and becomes a monk.
sentences.zh: 就是那个后来去当了修士的卡洛曼。

sentences.en: But the younger Carloman and his elder brother, Charles, so the sons of Pepin, they don't like each other at all.
sentences.zh: 但年轻的卡洛曼和他的哥哥查理，也就是丕平的儿子们，他们一点也不喜欢对方。

sentences.en: And Pepin's lands have been divided up between the two of them.
sentences.zh: 丕平的土地被分给了他们两人。

sentences.en: Charles gets this kind of half doughnut and Carloman gets the kind of lump in the middle.
sentences.zh: 查理得到了一半，卡洛曼得到了中间的一块。

sentences.en: They really don't get on well at all.
sentences.zh: 他们确实相处得非常不好。

sentences.en: And Einhard, in his account, he blames this on Carloman's advisors.
sentences.zh: 艾因哈德在他的记述中，将此归咎于卡洛曼的顾问们。

sentences.en: So he says that harmony between them was maintained, but only with difficulty.
sentences.zh: 他说，他们之间的和谐关系得以维持，但非常困难。

sentences.en: For many of Carloman's advisors did their best to foster divisions between the two brothers
sentences.zh: 因为卡洛曼的许多顾问竭尽全力在两兄弟之间制造分歧，

sentences.en: to the degree that some of them were actively manoeuvring to precipitate an open conflict.
sentences.zh: 以至于其中一些人积极策划引发公开冲突。

sentences.en: But then, in December 771, so that's only three years after the death of Pepin, a dramatic development, Carloman dies of a nosebleed.
sentences.zh: 但随后，在771年12月，也就是丕平去世仅三年后，发生了戏剧性的一幕，卡洛曼死于鼻出血。

sentences.en: Can you die of a nosebleed?
sentences.zh: 人会因为鼻出血而死吗？

sentences.en: I mean, well, clearly you can.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然是可以的。

sentences.en: I mean, was there foul play?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这里面有猫腻吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There doesn't seem to be in the sources any suspicion of that.
sentences.zh: 在史料中似乎并没有对此产生怀疑。

sentences.en: And I think most historians accept that it wasn't a nosebleed.
sentences.zh: 我认为大多数历史学家都接受他并非死于鼻出血。

sentences.en: I mean, he seems to have died of natural causes.
sentences.zh: 他似乎是死于自然原因。

sentences.en: And that means, of course, that Charles is now really the only kid on the block.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，当然，查理现在成了唯一的掌权者。

sentences.en: And he gets unanimously elected as king of all the lands of the Franks.
sentences.zh: 他被一致推选为所有法兰克领土的国王。

sentences.en: And so he now has the reins of this vast empire that's been forged by his father and his grandfather.
sentences.zh: 现在，他掌握了由他父亲和祖父锻造的这个庞大帝国的缰绳。

sentences.en: He alone holds the reins in his hands.
sentences.zh: 他独自一人掌握着缰绳。

sentences.en: And the question is, you know, as we said, what's he going to do with it?
sentences.zh: 问题是，正如我们所说，他会用它做什么呢？

sentences.en: He's so primed, so ready to go on the offensive.
sentences.zh: 他已经准备就绪，随时准备发动进攻。

sentences.en: And the question is, how far will he go?
sentences.zh: 问题是，他会走多远？

sentences.en: And I guess that there's a clue to the answer to that question in the name by which this new young king of the Franks, Charles, is best known today.
sentences.zh: 我想，这个年轻的法兰克新国王查理如今最广为人知的名字，或许能为那个问题的答案提供线索。

sentences.en: Because he is known by us, not as Charles, not as Charles, but as Charlemagne, Charles the Great.
sentences.zh: 因为我们所知的他，不是查理，不是查理，而是查理曼，即伟大的查理。

sentences.en: And in the next two episodes, we will be looking at how Charles earns that name.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的两集里，我们将探讨查理是如何赢得这个称号的。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。
